name: toyota_a25a_fks_gen
source: I7c C17a M-A generated-map engine: Toyota A25A-FKS 2.5 L I4 (2018 Camry) as a C15a cycle-model description; the runtime maps are GENERATED at load time by the C16a map generator (no 'maps' block). Validated against the US EPA NVFEL A25A Tier 3 dyno data it was never fitted to (tests/validation/test_gen_engine_dyno.cpp). Written by tools/enginedata/a25a_gen_engine.py. Idle/limiter/starter/DFCO/idle-PI facts are the same engine facts as data/engines/toyota_a25a_fks_sim.json (M-B) and copied from it.
geometry_source: bore 87.5 mm, stroke 103.4 mm, compression ratio 13.0 ([C] SAE 2019-01-0249 Table 1, used by the cycle block): secondary web sources (Toyota press material as quoted by third-party sites; see out/a25a/a25a_tables.json bore_stroke_note), not a primary citation
intake_manifold_volume_source: [AS] Tier 3: plenum = 1.2 x V_d (2.48706 L) (i7c plan rule; runners not added).
throttle_body_source: [AS] Tier 3: bore sized for a 60 m/s mean air velocity at 6600 rpm (Toyota's rated-power SPEED [C]) with VE 1 at ISA [rule of thumb, recalled]. DISCLOSURE: the M-B file's air-flow-sized 53.6171 mm bore had been seen before this rule was applied. Cd 0.8 [AS] and the area-fraction shape above position 0 [AS] are the M-B file's. y(0) [D] = 0.5 x the plate-0 leak area fraction giving zero net torque at idle_rpm 800 (ISA) on this engine's OWN generated maps (model-consistency rule, as M-B; measured by the [.][diag] case 'C17a-MA diag: idle leak bisection'), so the idle PI keeps authority.
throttle_actuator_source: [AS] assumed 50 ms first-order electronic throttle actuator (as the C11 test fixture)

lambda_target.source: [D] Tier 1b: measured exhaust lambda per fired point, gridded (IDW k6, nearest outside the measured hull) by a25a_author.py; raw, protective-enrichment WOT points kept

ecu_source: ecu.spark_advance_deg is not given here: the loader takes it from cycle.spark_advance_deg (the measured schedule the generator ran its nodes at; C17a follow-up).

cycle.source: I7c C17a M-A: C15a 0D cycle-model description of the Toyota A25A-FKS; the loader generates every runtime map from it (C16a). Tiers per i7c plan D1: Tier 1 = measured/cited engine description, Tier 1b = measured ECU schedules (inputs only), Tier 2 = literature constants frozen before any comparison, Tier 3 = [AS] geometry set by a stated sizing rule. Nothing here was chosen from the A25A's measured torque, fuel flow, BSFC, air flow, WOT envelope or motoring curve. Gas properties: the descriptor's defaults (NIST-JANAF linear cv fits [Tier 2, DERIVED], ps/drivetrain/engine_cycle_desc.h). Not modelled: intake manifold temperature (charge at ambient), exhaust back pressure (I7d), EGR (plan D3; the EPA data show the EGR valve closed along WOT above ~2000 rpm).
cycle.rod_mm_source: [AS] Tier 3: l/r = 3.0 (low end of the 3-4 range for small SI engines, Heywood 1988 sec. 2.2 [recalled, page to verify]; low end because of the long stroke) x crank radius 51.7 mm. No A25A rod length found.
cycle.pin_offset_mm_source: [C] Tier 1: crankshaft offset 10.1 mm, SAE 2019-01-0249 Table 1. Sign [AS]: positive = the rod stands closer to the cylinder axis during the expansion stroke (the purpose of a desaxe crank), geometry.h's convention.
cycle.intake_valve_d_mm_source: [AS] Tier 3: head diameters 0.36 x bore (intake) and 0.3 x bore (exhaust), the midpoints of the 4-valve pent-roof ranges 0.35-0.37 / 0.28-0.32 of Heywood 1988 Table 6.2 [recalled, page to verify].
cycle.intake_lift_source: [D] Tier 1: SAE 2019-01-0249 Fig. 11 (reproduced in the EPA NVFEL A25A test report) digitised by hand at phase 0 on a 2 deg grid (out/a25a/a25a_tables.json valve_lift_fig11, read uncertainty 0.3 mm / 5 deg); each curve is taken between its bounding 0 mm samples, x relative to the first; phase_ref = that first sample in the 0..720 frame. The SAE text's theta_VO(1 mm) = 138.6 deg disagrees with the figure's 1 mm opening crossing (~68 deg); the figure is used.
cycle.runner_length_mm_source: [AS] Tier 3, quarter-wave ram rule: the runner's quarter-wave period 4L/a equals the intake-open time (240 deg, the digitised lift start/end read points) at 4800 rpm (Toyota's rated peak-torque speed [C], the speed only), a = sqrt(1.4*287.05*288.15) = 340.29 m/s.
cycle.runner_diameter_mm_source: [AS] Tier 3: runner flow area = the total intake valve head area.
cycle.intake_port_cc_source: [AS] Tier 3: 80 mm port length x the total intake valve head area; 250 mm (port plus the short 4-into-1 primary [C: integrated exhaust manifold]) x the total exhaust valve head area.
cycle.cd_vs_l_over_d_source: [AS] Tier 2: discharge coefficient on the curtain area falling with L/D as in Heywood 1988 Fig. 6-19 [recalled, page to verify]; the C15a test fixture's curve, frozen before any comparison; clamped beyond L/D 0.3.

intake_advance_deg.source: [D] Tier 1b: measured icam_adv_deg per fired point, gridded (IDW k6, nearest outside the measured hull) by a25a_author.py, then a running median of 3 along MAP per rpm row repeated to its root signal (DERIVED, see cam_source); reaches 55 deg (above the cited 0-50 deg spec, kept as measured)

exhaust_retard_deg.source: [D] Tier 1b: measured ecam_ret_deg per fired point, gridded as above, same median-of-3 root smoothing along MAP

cycle.cam_source: [D] Tier 1b: the EPA-measured cam phase schedules, inputs only (never fitted). DERIVED smoothing: the raw IDW grid made the cycle model's trapped air fall with rising MAP at 600/800/1000 rpm (by up to 6.4 %; nearest-neighbour cam steps of up to 24 deg exhaust retard between adjacent MAP cells), which the generator rejects (eta_i is resampled over air mass). Chosen from that model-side criterion only, before any dyno comparison: 47/240 intake and 55/240 exhaust cells change; smallest air step after it +7.6 %.

spark_advance_deg.source: [D] Tier 1b: measured 'Spark Timing, CAD BTDC' per fired point (EPA NVFEL A25A Tier 3 xlsx), gridded (IDW k6, nearest outside the measured hull) by a25a_author.py's build_schedule_grid, then the cam tables' median-3 root along MAP (DERIVED; see spark_advance_deg_source)

cycle.spark_advance_deg_source: [D] Tier 1b (C17a follow-up, owner ruling 1): the EPA-measured ECU spark schedule, an input only (never fitted); 240 measured points, 98/240 cells outside their hull (nearest value). The 30 protection-enrichment rows are kept (real ECU behaviour, as in lambda_target); 28/240 cells have one as their nearest sample (schedules.protection_enrichment_flag_grid). The generator runs every grid node at this spark; it is also the ECU's runtime schedule (the loader copies it into ecu.spark_advance_deg). DERIVED smoothing, chosen before any dyno comparison: with the raw grid the runtime rejects the engine (steady torque falls with plate by 0.49 N*m at 2750 rpm, p 96-97 kPa, where the raw grid retards 18.2 -> -0.8 deg BTDC between the 89.5 and 97.3 kPa cells at 2700 rpm); the cam tables' parameter-free median-3 root along MAP keeps the WOT column and monotone runs and changes 49/240 cells by up to 20.07 deg (isolated nearest-neighbour excursions at 600-1000 rpm; 97.3 kPa by <= 1.35 deg at 1200-3300 rpm).
cycle.wiebe_source: Tier 2: Wiebe a 5, m 2 (Heywood 1988 sec. 9.2.1); CA50 at MBT 8 deg ATDC (plan D11 MBT rule). Burn duration and ignition delay: the burn law (design C, owner decision 2026-10-19, vault PHYS-079; ps/engine_cycle/burn_law.h, data/burn_laws/default.json) sets both per cycle from the cycle's own IVC state; at the law's reference state they are the C17a [D] values 40.3205 / 3.8632 deg derived from MIT 2.61 lecture 9 (vault PHYS-055), which this file carried as constants before the law.
cycle.woschni_source: Tier 2: Woschni 1967 as given by Heywood 1988 sec. 12.4.3.
cycle.wall_temperature_k_source: [AS] Tier 2: descriptor defaults (wall 450 K, pent-roof head area 1.1 x bore area, backflow gas 800 K), frozen.
cycle.combustion_eff_lean_source: Tier 2: plan D14 (eta_c 0.98 at lambda >= 1, x lambda below).
cycle.friction_source: Tier 2, plan D13 option F4: FMEP = a + b*s + c*s^2 kPa over mean piston speed s, FITTED ON A THIRD ENGINE (the EPA NVFEL 2013 Chevrolet 2.5 L Ecotec LCV motored rows, pumping subtracted with the C15a fixture's ASSUMED valvetrain), not on the A25A. Known bias: low at high speed (tests/unit/test_engine_map_generator.cpp).
cycle.grid_source: plan default: the Tier 1b schedule grid (600-6900 rpm x 20-105 kPa).

fields_source: Copied from data/engines/toyota_a25a_fks_sim.json (the same engine facts): [AS] inertia 0.16 kg*m^2, breakaway 45 N*m (>= the F4 friction at 0 rpm, ~13.2 N*m), stall/fire/start_complete 400/250/550 rpm, DFCO 1300/1000 rpm, starter 140 N*m/400 rpm (as data/engines/i4_2l_na.json, no A25A measurement); idle_rpm 800 [AS] (the measured cell idle rows sit at 590-663 rpm under dyno load); idle PI kp 3e-5 /rpm, ki 6e-5 /(rpm*s), max plate 0.1 [AS] (the C11 fixture's); limiter fuel_cut 6500 rpm / 150 rpm [AS] = the cited EPA test-cell limit [C] (Report 26781 Table 5) - PROVISIONAL, 6600 rpm is Toyota's rated-power speed, not a cut. Fuels: tier3_e10_cert burnt (the fuel the EPA data were measured on), e10 selectable.
